message.content:
Answer: A
Reason: Primary pulmonary MALT lymphoma classically presents on chest X-ray as bilateral, persistent airspace consolidations that frequently contain air bronchograms, mimicking pneumonia but failing to resolve with antibiotics. The other options (cavitation, significant lymphadenopathy, pleural effusion) are more characteristic of infections, high-grade lymphomas, or other malignancies rather than indolent MALT lymphoma.
